newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal unhappy at British arms for Indonesia.
newsitem.headline: Portugal unhappy at British arms for Indonesia.

text.p: Portugal's Prime Minister Antonio Guterres rang Britain's Tony Blair on Thursday to express his government's "displeasure" at continuing British sales of military planes to Indonesia.
The British premier reaffirmed his Labour government would ban future arms sales to countries with a poor record on human rights, Guterres' office said in a statement.
But the Indonesian deal had already been agreed by the previous Conservative administration, it quoted Blair as telling Guterres, a fellow Socialist.
Britain announced on Monday it would clamp down on weapons' sales to countries where they might be used for internal repression.
But it refused to withdraw thousands of existing defence contracts, including one for 16 British Aerospace Hawk jets and armoured vehicles to Indonesia.
Human rights activists say that the planes have been used against resistance groups in East Timor, the former Portuguese colony annexed by Indonesia after a bloody invasion in 1975.
The United Nations has never recognised Indonesia's sovereignty over the territory and has been attempting to broker talks between Jakarta and Lisbon on its future.
